## Big idea

Build a small REST API with clear layers. Do not put everything in one class.

```text
Client (browser / Postman)
        │  HTTP
        ▼
   Controller   ← talk to HTTP only
        │
        ▼
   Service      ← business rules
        │
        ▼
   Repository   ← data access (later: JPA)
        │
        ▼
   Database / in-memory list (for now)
```

## Layers (plain words)

| Layer | Job | Typical annotation |
|-------|-----|--------------------|
| Controller | Accept HTTP, return JSON | `@RestController` |
| Service | Business logic | `@Service` |
| Repository | Save / load data | `@Repository` (or interface later) |
| Entity / model | Shape of the data | plain class / `@Entity` later |

**Rule:** Controller should not talk to the database directly.

## Practice — in-memory product API

1. Boot project + **Web** starter.
2. Model:

```java
public class Product {
    private Long id;
    private String name;
    private double price;
    // constructors, getters, setters
}
```

3. Service with a `List<Product>` and methods: create, getAll, getById, update, delete.
4. Controller:

```java
@RestController
@RequestMapping("/api/products")
public class ProductController {
    private final ProductService service;
    public ProductController(ProductService service) { this.service = service; }

    @GetMapping
    public List<Product> all() { return service.getAll(); }

    @GetMapping("/{id}")
    public Product one(@PathVariable Long id) { return service.getById(id); }

    @PostMapping
    public Product create(@RequestBody Product p) { return service.create(p); }

    @PutMapping("/{id}")
    public Product update(@PathVariable Long id, @RequestBody Product p) {
        return service.update(id, p);
    }

    @DeleteMapping("/{id}")
    public void delete(@PathVariable Long id) { service.delete(id); }
}
```

5. Test with Postman or curl.

## Reasoning

- Why layers? So you can change storage later without rewriting HTTP code.
- Why constructor injection? Required deps are clear and easy to test.
